audit.whatIsWrong: The page called Hwei's CC palette "Subject: Fear (CC Paints)" in eleven fields. Hwei has no such ability. Content also invented "Fated Fates" and "Severed Mind".
audit.why: Kit file: P Signature of the Visionary, Q Subject: Disaster (Devastating Fire, Severing Bolt, Molten Fissure), W Subject: Serenity (Fleeting Current, Pool of Reflection, Stirring Lights), E Subject: Torment (Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw), R Spiraling Despair.
audit.corrected: Every reachable instance renamed to Subject: Torment, "Severed Mind" to Severing Bolt, and "Fated Fates" replaced with a real description of Spiraling Despair.

audit.why: phases[0..6].side and win[0..6] both read Galio 7/7 and match packet.levelChart, so no cross-layer disagreement exists to fix. The packet separately flags that this chart contradicts a 44.87% win rate — see notes and questionsForUser; I did not flip rows on a win rate alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and no spike text carried a Hwei cooldown.
audit.why: Subject: Torment is 12s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5; Subject: Serenity is 18s; Spiraling Despair is 120s at rank 1 with 1300 range. Those numbers are the whole timing of the lane.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field and three bullets now carry them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentioned that Subject: Serenity shields the burst you commit into.
audit.why: missingInteractions shield-absorbs-burst, confirmed by the W shield flag and Riot's utility-palette text.
audit.corrected: Now stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[0].d and wants.foe[2].

edits.before: Refund the poke war with MR math and tax the map with R. Track Subject: Fear (CC Paints) before every commit and keep the wave where your pattern works.
edits.after: Refund the poke war with MR math and tax the map with R. Track Subject: Torment (CC Paints) before every commit and keep the wave where your pattern works.

edits.before: Hwei wins by landing Subject: Fear (CC Paints), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Hwei wins by catching you with the Subject: Torment palette, completing his signature for the detonation, and never letting you close.

edits.before: - Galio vs Hwei - Track: Hwei Subject: Fear (CC Paints). - Trade behind the shield — the passive is the matchup vs AP. - Engage only on Subject: Fear (CC Paints)’s cooldown. - Spend your ultimate on kill windows only.
edits.after: - Galio vs Hwei - Track: Hwei Subject: Torment (CC Paints). - Trade behind the shield — the passive is the matchup vs AP. - Engage only on Subject: Torment (CC Paints)’s cooldown. - Spend your ultimate on kill windows only.

edits.before: - Hwei Subject: Fear (CC Paints): matchup-defining — All his crowd control lives on the E palette — dodge the fear/root and the burst never chains. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Shield of Durand for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Subject: Torment (E): 12s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5 — every piece of his crowd control lives on that palette, so once it is spent you have ten seconds to walk in. - Spiraling Despair: 120s at rank 1. - Subject: Serenity is 18s and shields the burst you were counting on.

edits.before: If Hwei gets one kill, respect Subject: Fear (CC Paints) and reset to farming. Two kills: play for the team, not for solo redemption — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through taunt peel and R arrivals.
edits.after: If Hwei gets one kill, respect Subject: Torment (CC Paints) and reset to farming. Two kills: play for the team, not for solo redemption — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through taunt peel and R arrivals.

edits.before: All his crowd control lives on the E palette — dodge the fear/root and the burst never chains. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: His crowd control is all on Subject: Torment, a 12-second palette — the moment he casts from another one, your step-up is free.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Hwei's passive only detonates after a second damaging spell, so the taunt to look for is the follow-up cast, not the opener.

edits.before: Hwei wastes Subject: Fear (CC Paints) — that is your full-commit window.
edits.after: Hwei wastes Subject: Torment (CC Paints) — that is your full-commit window.

edits.before: That’s Hwei’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Subject: Serenity is an 18s shield that eats the poke you traded for.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: Justice Punch on a 9-second cooldown is your only way through his 1300-range poke — spend it on minions and you eat the palette.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by ending his sequence: his passive needs a second spell to detonate, and a taunt mid-palette costs him the combo.

edits.before: Refund the poke war with MR math and tax the map with R. Track Subject: Fear (CC Paints) before every commit and keep the wave where your pattern works.
edits.after: Refund the poke war with MR math and tax the map with R. Track Subject: Torment (CC Paints) before every commit and keep the wave where your pattern works.

edits.before: Track Hwei’s Subject: Fear (CC Paints): All his crowd control lives on the E palette — dodge the fear/root and the burst never chains. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Hwei’s Subject: Torment (E): every piece of his crowd control lives on that palette — cast from another and your step-up is free. It’s down or you don’t go.

edits.before: Hwei's Devastating Fire and Severed Mind combos need long cast times you can dodge with movement, and your Q-into-E closing speed punishes him hard whenever he whiffs a combo piece.
edits.after: Hwei's Devastating Fire and Severing Bolt combos need long cast times you can dodge with movement, and your Q-into-E closing speed punishes him hard whenever he whiffs a combo piece.

edits.before: Fated Fates gives Hwei a strong disengage or a combo-extending stun on the smallest painting, but landing it into a real combo requires precision your all-in pressure disrupts.
edits.after: Spiraling Despair is a 1300-range painting that sticks to the first champion it hits and slows nearby enemies, but landing it into a real combo requires precision your all-in pressure disrupts.

edits.before: Kite using Devastating Fire's slow zone to keep distance
edits.after: Kite using Molten Fissure's slow zone to keep distance

edits.before: Save Fated Fates disengage for your all-in attempts
edits.after: Save Subject: Serenity's shield for your all-ins

notes: THREE fabricated ability names on one matchup: 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' (his E is Subject: Torment), 'Fated Fates' and 'Severed Mind' (Severing Bolt). All reachable instances are fixed here. STILL WRONG and out of reach under the two-per-matchup report cap: report[3].t and report[9].t both still say 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' — they need the same Torment rename in a later pass. I kept the '(CC Paints)' parenthetical because it follows the AbilityName (Effect) convention and is accurate for that palette. No chart edits: sides, win[] and packet.levelChart all agree at Galio 7/7 — but see questionsForUser, because a 7/7 sweep sits badly against a 44.87% win rate over 2231 games and the diff/diffRating currently read FAVOURED 4/10. Molten Fissure as the slowing zone of the Subject: Disaster palette is inferred from the Q slow+zone flags rather than stated in Riot's text — medium confidence.
